messages:
Amira (PM): Quick sync — we're finalizing the PRD + rollout plan for the "auto-fallback" model routing feature. Need consensus on acceptance gates, experiment design, and the scope tradeoffs customers asked for. TL;DR: allow per-tenant version pin, but enable automatic fallback to a compatible thinner/quantized variant on capacity or perf regressions.

Jae (Eng-Platform): +1. Can you call out the hard SLOs we need for canary before we enable auto-fallback?

Amira (PM): Initial thoughts:
- Launch acceptance: 99th perc latency <= 150ms for 95% of requests on dedicated SKU, error rate < 0.5% on host inference.
- Experiment success: 0.5% or less difference in subjective quality (eval prompts) between baseline and fallback at 95% CI.
- Rollback triggers: any increase in customer-facing error rate > 1% absolute or latency regressions > 30% p95 sustained for 10m.

Carmen (SRE): Those look reasonable. Suggest making the error-rate rollback trigger relative to the tenant baseline (e.g., +50% from baseline) rather than absolute, because smaller customers have noisy baselines.

Sasha (Growth): Important we track user-facing engagement signals (CTA click-through, completion length) as secondary metrics in A/B. Can't rely on model-labeled evals alone.

Tom (ML Infra): From infra side, the primary technical constraint is model compatibility for KV cache and max sequence length. We should precompute compatibility matrix and only allow fallback to variants with identical tokenization and sequence length support.

Amira (PM): Good catch. Let's make compatibility a hard constraint in the rollout policy. Draft experiment config (very rough):
```yaml
experiment: auto-fallback-v1
variants:
  - control: baseline-model-v2
  - treatment: baseline-model-v2 + fallback-policy
traffic_split: 50/50
metrics:
  - primary: customer_error_rate
  - primary: p95_latency
  - secondary: user_cta_rate
rollout_checks:
  - duration: 72h
  - min_requests_per_tenant: 1k
  - rollback_on: >50% relative error increase OR p95_latency >30%
```

Priya (QA): For the 72h window we should also mandate manual sign-off for any tenant with regulatory constraints (e.g., private deployments). Auto-fallback should be opt-in for Private.

Jae (Eng-Platform): Agreed. Private deployments must be explicit opt-in. For Hosted, default to opt-out. Also, how do we handle version pinning? If tenant pins to baseline-model-v2, do we still auto-fallback?

Amira (PM): Proposal: pin semantics = "hard pin" (no fallback) or "soft pin" (allows fallback under SLA-preserving conditions). Default pinning behavior will be soft for hosted customers, hard for Dedicated & Private unless customer requests otherwise. We need a clear UI flag and API field.

Tom (ML Infra): Implementation note: hard pin means we will not route to fallback variants and must throttle/respond with 429 when capacity exhausted (or queue). Soft pin will allow fallback but we must surface to tenant telemetry that a fallback occurred (token-level logs + reason).

Carmen (SRE): On the 429 vs fallback decision — I recommend fallback-first for latency-sensitive customers and 429 for customers who opted into strict model fidelity. Add a new per-tenant policy: failure_mode = [fallback | reject].

Sasha (Growth): For experiment slicing, we should stratify by tenant size and workload (chat vs. single-turn) to avoid confounding. Growth wants a separate cohort of high-frequency tenants excluded from early experiments.

Amira (PM): Good catch. Add strata: small (<50 req/min), medium (50-500), large (>500), and workload type. Also include a "no-experiment" list for top 20 enterprise tenants.

Priya (QA): Edge cases to add to PRD:
- Edge: tokenization mismatch between model variants => block fallback.
- Edge: stateful sessions across versions (chat KV cache) => only allow fallback at session boundary unless KV compatibility is verified.
- Edge: cold-start latency for fallback model when not already cached. Must measure tail latencies.

Jae (Eng-Platform): For canary gating, I propose automated checks + manual override:
1) Automated checks run every 15m on global metrics and per-strata metrics.
2) If any automated check trips, system will alert oncall and pause the experiment; manual approval required to resume.

Carmen (SRE): Make sure alerts are actionable: include sample failing tenants, stack traces, and a quick runbook. devops-bot should post to #incidents and #product with a summary.

devops-bot: [deploy] experiment auto-fallback-v1 started on 1799033333 by Amira (PM) :rocket:

Tom (ML Infra): Can we add an early-warning micro-metric for quality drift: average log-likelihood delta on a fixed eval set per tenant? That detects subtle regressions before user metrics change.

Sasha (Growth): Yes, we can use that as an early-warning but not as a final gate. Growth wants to see downstream behavior changes for at least 48h before we call it successful.

Amira (PM): Acceptance criteria (final draft):
- Safety: No tenant experiences >50% relative increase in error rate or >30% p95 latency within experiment window.
- Quality: Delta on held-out eval set < 0.5% absolute in surrogate metrics, and user CTA delta < 1% (95% CI).
- Observability: Fallback events surfaced in tenant logs, per-request annotation, and dashboard.
- Controls: Hard pin honored; Private deployments opt-in only; top-20 enterprises excluded by default.

Priya (QA): I can write the test matrix for QA: unit tests for routing logic, integration tests simulating capacity pressure, e2e with session-boundary fallbacks, and chaos test forcing model crash.

Jae (Eng-Platform): Timeline ask: can infra deliver compatibility matrix + routing config API in 3 sprints? If yes, we can start a small closed experiment in 6 weeks.

Tom (ML Infra): 3 sprints is tight but doable if we scope compatibility matrix to current model family first (no new architectures). We'll need 1 sprint for infra + 2 for validation and dashboards.

Amira (PM): OK. Owners:
- PRD + acceptance criteria: Amira
- Compatibility matrix + routing API: Tom + Jae
- Observability & alerts: Carmen + Jae
- Experiment design and metrics: Sasha + Priya
- QA tests and sign-off: Priya

Amira (PM): Next steps: I'll update PRD with these gates and a short rollout playbook. Please add any missing rollback conditions or experiments here. If no objections, I'll put this up for RFC review tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

Sasha (Growth): One more ask: include a comms plan for any tenant experiencing fallback — auto-email + console banner explaining what changed and how to opt-out.

Amira (PM): Noted. Will add comms + self-serve opt-out.

Jae (Eng-Platform): No objections from platform.

Carmen (SRE): No objections. Add PS/Support runbook before wide rollout.

Tom (ML Infra): 👍 ready to start on infra tickets.

Priya (QA): I'll draft the test matrix and link it into PRD by EOD tomorrow.

Amira (PM): Thanks everyone — will share updated PRD + RFC link in this thread when ready. :pray:
